items.review_rationale: Read normality via splitting over E of every element's minimal polynomial over F, preserving that the extension is algebraic and the roots are required to lie in E; not equivalent to every polynomial over F splitting.

references.phrase: minimal polynomial of α over F
factors completely into linear factors over E
references.context: Field theory: polynomial splitting as a product of degree-one factors in E[x]

references.disposition: Only the minimal polynomials of extension elements are quantified, not every polynomial in F[x].

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the 2-fibre-product test for every base object U and morphism C/U→Y, requiring the pullback fibred groupoid to be representable over U. This is relative representability of a 1-morphism, not representability of X alone.

references.phrase: categories fibred in groupoids X,Y over C

references.context: Category theory: overcategory of all arrows into U, with morphisms commuting over U
Higher category theory: functor over C from the slice category to fibred groupoid Y

references.disposition: The universal base-change test must range over every object and such map; a single fibre test is not sufficient.

items.review_rationale: Read the coequalizer as a topological quotient of Y by the least equivalence relation identifying f(x) with g(x) for all x, with quotient topology; separate the categorical coequalizer property from the quotient equivalence closure.

references.context: Set theory: smallest equivalence relation on Y containing prescribed pairs
Topology: final topology induced by canonical surjection from Y to quotient set

references.disposition: The relation is generated by all prescribed pairs, not necessarily only those pairs without transitive closure.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed disjoint-union construction and precise componentwise openness condition for a possibly indexed family of topological spaces; this is not the ordinary topology on a set-theoretic union when underlying sets overlap.

references.context: Set theory: tagged disjoint union indexed by i, retaining identity of each component
Topology: a subset U of coproduct is open if and only if all intersections U∩X_i are open in X_i

references.disposition: No finiteness of the indexing family or compatibility between component topologies is assumed.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed requirement that closure of every open U of X is open in X; do not mistake this for total disconnectedness or the weaker property that closures of closed sets remain closed.

references.phrase: open subset U of topological space
references.context: Topology: membership in the topology on X

references.phrase: closure(U) is open for every open U
references.disposition: The universal quantifier is over all open subsets; it does not say every subset has open closure.

items.review_rationale: Read the relative-assassin construction at prime q over p=q∩R, including the fibre module N⊗_R κ(p) and associated-prime condition; do not confuse p in Spec(R) with q in Spec(S).

references.phrase: residue field κ(p) of R at p
references.context: Commutative algebra: fraction field of residue ring R_p/pR_p at prime p
Commutative algebra: inverse-image prime of q along ring homomorphism R→S

references.phrase: equivalently q is an associated prime of fibre module
references.disposition: The associated-prime test is carried out on the fibre module with correct scalar ring action; it does not simply require q∈Ass_S(N) before base change.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed closure incidence condition for a partition into locally closed strata: if X_i meets cl(X_j), then the whole X_i lies in cl(X_j), rather than merely having nonempty intersection.

references.context: Topology: intersection of a locally closed stratum with closure of another

references.phrase: if intersection nonempty then entire X_i is contained
references.disposition: The condition is asymmetric and must hold for every pair of strata, not a symmetric adjacency condition.

items.review_rationale: Read all requirements for a partition of X: components X_i locally closed in X, pairwise disjoint, and collectively cover all of X. Do not require finiteness or locally finite indexing unless separately specified.

references.context: Topology: subset equal to intersection of an open and closed subset of X
Set theory: pairwise disjoint subsets indexed by I whose union equals X

references.phrase: all of X covered and pieces pairwise disjoint
references.disposition: No finiteness, ordering, or local finiteness of the family is required by this formulation.
